findings.title: Interpolating before querySupportsSplitting defeats the $__range no-splitting guard
findings.body: runSplitQuery now interpolates every target via datasource.applyTemplateVariables (line 299) before partition(queries, (query) => !querySupportsSplitting(query)) runs on the next line. applyTemplateVariables substitutes the built-in range variables ($__range, $__range_s, $__range_ms) from scopedVars, and dashboard/Explore requests always carry those scoped vars. querySupportsSplitting() decides a query must not be split by calling isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr), which searches for the literal text '$__range' — but by the time it runs, that text has already been replaced (e.g. count_over_time({a="b"}[$__range]) has become count_over_time({a="b"}[30d])). Consequence: queries using $__range are now time-split instead of being routed to nonSplittingQueries and executed once over the full range, which is exactly what the comment above the check says must not happen. Besides contradicting the documented intent, this is a real cost/correctness regression for large ranges: with a 30-day dashboard, each 1-day chunk evaluates count_over_time(...[30d]), re-scanning ~30 days of data per chunk (~30x the scanned volume of the previous single request). The existing unit tests do not catch this because the test requests carry no scopedVars, so $__range survives interpolation in tests but not in production. The isQueryWithRangeVariable check should run on the raw, pre-interpolation expr — or, if splitting such queries is now intentional, the dead check and its misleading comment should be removed.

findings.title: Queries are now interpolated two to three times (runShardSplitQuery / runSplitQuery / runQuery)
findings.body: Interpolation is now applied repeatedly to the same targets. LokiDatasource.runQuery — which the splitting code calls for every sub-request (runSplitGroupedQueries in querySplitting.ts, and splitQueriesByStreamShard here) — already maps targets through applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters). With the new .map(...) added here in runShardSplitQuery and the one added in runSplitQuery (querySplitting.ts), every sub-query in the time-splitting path is interpolated twice, and every sub-query in the shard-splitting path three times (runShardSplitQuery → runSplitQuery → runQuery), because sub-requests keep the original request.scopedVars and request.filters. Two concrete consequences: (1) ad hoc filters from request.filters are injected into the stream selector on every pass, so the LogQL selectors sent to Loki contain each ad hoc matcher two or three times (previously they were injected exactly once, in runQuery); (2) any variable value that itself contains template syntax (a constant/text variable holding a literal containing another variable's name, or a $-prefixed token) is interpolated again by the later passes, silently altering the query Loki executes. The updated shard-splitting test that expects applyTemplateVariables to have been called 5 times for a single-target request (1 call in runShardSplitQuery plus 1 per shard group in runSplitQuery, with runQuery mocked) shows the redundancy is being baked into the tests rather than eliminated. One of the interpolation layers should be removed (or the later passes skipped for already-interpolated targets).
